sourceBlog.title: Korea's ARC, Phone, Bank Loop: The Fix

introSlide.heading: 5 things everyone gets wrong about settling in Korea
introSlide.description: The ARC, phone, bank loop is real. This is the 4-week sequence.

slides.heading: ❌ MYTH: You can open a bank account on day 1
slides.description: Reality: You need an ARC and a Korean phone number first. Expect 3-4 weeks.

slides.heading: ❌ MYTH: Any SIM card works for banking
slides.description: eSIMs give data only, no Korean number. You need a physical prepaid SIM (+82 010).

slides.heading: ✅ FACT: Mobile ARC works for banking now
slides.description: Since Jan 2025, the digital ARC on your phone is accepted. No plastic card needed.

slides.heading: ❌ MYTH: Online banking works right away
slides.description: Identity verification (본인인증) needs a postpaid plan. Prepaid won’t cut it.

slides.heading: ❌ MYTH: B-2 tourists can open a bank account
slides.description: No ARC, no account. Use WOWPASS instead: it’s the practical workaround for short stays.

slides.heading: The real sequence, week by week
slides.description: Day 1: prepaid SIM. Day 7: ARC apply. Day 14: mobile ARC. Day 21: bank. Day 28: postpaid.

caption:
Most people land in Korea and assume they can sort out a bank account in the first week. That’s not how it works.

The setup runs in a fixed sequence: get a physical prepaid SIM on day 1 (eSIM won’t give you a Korean number), apply for your ARC within the first week, pick up your mobile ARC around day 14, then open a bank account around day 21. Postpaid phone, which unlocks full identity verification (본인인증), comes last, around week 4.

Short-stay on a B-2 visa? Skip the bank. WOWPASS covers most payment needs and doesn’t require an ARC. And since Jan 2025, if you do have an ARC, the digital version on your phone is accepted at banks, no physical card required.
